note: These are theorem/deployment assumptions, not extrema fitted from the eight reference replays. The physical COMPLETE-BRMM source is anchored to the Hs=8.5 m reference case and padded outward before P4 closure. Physical source bounds and estimator error-entry bounds are distinct objects.

configured_runtime.accelerometer_vibration_guard_note: PR #426 armed a 14 Hz stateful accelerometer prefilter by default. The pre-existing P1-P5 source model remains exact only on the source branch where its detector stays at or below the 0.03 m/s^2 lower engagement rail and the guard starts at zero engagement, for which shipping code returns the raw accelerometer bit-for-bit. Active/transitioning guard dynamics, impacts and slamming are separate source/hybrid proof obligations and are not promoted by this domain.

measurement_noise_std.source: SeaStateFusion_OU_III::Config defaults passed to Kalman3D_Wave_OU_III constructor

startup.online_tune_warmup_source: outer SeaStateFusion_OU_III::Config default forwarded by setOnlineTuneWarmupSec; overrides inner ONLINE_TUNE_WARMUP_SEC=5 s
startup.tuning_frequency_takeover_condition: WavePeriodEstimator::hasUsablePeriod(); does not wait for WavePeriodEstimator::isReady()
startup.wave_period_estimator_usable_time_floor_: 4/lambda plus at least one current estimated period of accumulated moment history
startup.physical_handoff_coordinate_bounds_role: legacy conditional diagnostic error box, not the physical wave-state envelope and not established fresh-wrapper reachability; use ou3_p4_live_entry_graph.py

sea_scaled_translation_coordinates.Ts_role: positive characteristic sea period used only as a coordinate scale unless a separate theorem bound is declared

initial_filter_entrance.note: The 45 deg attitude and |delta p_i| <= 0.5 Hs conditions are error entrance assumptions. The physical source envelope is separately padded from the 8.5 m reference sea to Hs<=9.35 m before P4 closure.

normal_live.specific_force_norm_definition: norm of CoG accelerometer model vector a_w-g before accelerometer bias/noise; lever arm disabled in this proof branch
normal_live.active_accelerometer_bias_interior_scope: auxiliary interior-only nonlinear certificates; not the primary bounded-bias theorem or covariance-only P3 algebra
normal_live.primary_bounded_bias_estimate_domain: closed projection ball of radius 0.4 m/s^2; nonlinear P4 boundary retention remains open

gravity_quotient.note: Conditional gravity-only theorem hypothesis: before magnetic regauging, every quotient word contains two accepted accelerometer packets separated inside the declared interval and satisfying the same padded 8.8 m/s^2 non-gravitational CoG acceleration envelope.

normal_live.pe_scope_note: The full-heading theorem is for normal ocean-wave/ship motion at the CoG, not impact/slam dynamics. Its primary padded physical acceleration assumption is ||a_non-grav|| <= 8.8 m/s^2. With g=9.80665 m/s^2 and lever arm disabled, triangle inequality gives 1.00665 <= ||a_w-g|| <= 18.60665 m/s^2. The 10 uT magnetic floor and 0.1 vector-sine separation remain PE assumptions. Active/transitioning vibration guard, impacts/slams, nonzero lever arm, and hard attitude rewrites remain separate hybrid/domain obligations. The primary bounded-bias theorem covers the closed estimate projection ball; P3 covariance identity at projection does not close nonlinear P4 retention.
normal_live.accelerometer_update_scope_note: After entry into Normal Live, every valid IMU sample executes the accelerometer Kalman update. The certified source language therefore contains no rejected/missing accelerometer branch; numerical innovation-factorization failure is outside the normal theorem domain. Magnetometer timing and rejection remain asynchronous.
normal_live.magnetic_reference_handling: source-generated world-reference/gauge variation is retained in the time-varying measurement vector or ISS forcing; it is not frozen to a replay value

stochastic.role_in_P3: noise realizations are ISS/finite-horizon forcing, not homogeneous-matrix pruning; configured Racc/Rmag remain in every Kalman covariance update
